title: Home Assistant
intro: Let your chats and agents read your smart home. If you allow it, they can also switch things, within the limits you set below.
limits: This connection does not answer messages. An agent works on your home only when you ask it in a chat.
name: Name
tokenHelp: Made in your Home Assistant profile. It is kept sealed and never shown again.
tokenSaved: Saved. Type a token to replace it.
tokenSpace: The token has no spaces. Copy it again without the spaces around it.
tokenShort: This is too short to be a long-lived access token. Copy the whole token.
addressHelp: Where you open Home Assistant in a browser, for example https://homeassistant.local:8123. One connection is one home. Any other address is refused.
addressShape: This is not an address. Write it as https://name:8123.
addressHttp: Plain http is accepted only for an address on your own network. Use https for anything else.
agentOptionalHint: Optional. Without an agent this connection only holds the token, the address and the write mode for your chats. It answers no messages and listens for nothing.
checkSeveral: The check of the address runs when you have one Home Assistant connection, because a check from this page cannot tell which one you mean. In a chat, enable the connections in the Tools menu.

check.title: Check of {{name}}
check.refused: Home Assistant refused this token. Check that it was not deleted and that it belongs to a user who can see what you want to share.
check.certificate: The certificate is not trusted. If it is self-signed, pin its fingerprint below.
check.failed: The check did not finish. Check the address and try again in a moment.

noAddress: No address: this connection reaches nothing.

confirmDelete.title: Delete {{name}}?
confirmDelete.message: Your chats can no longer reach this home, and the token saved with it is deleted. To set it up again you must enter the token again.

setup.title: How to make the token
setup.step1: In Home Assistant, open your profile (your name at the bottom of the sidebar) and then the Security tab.
setup.step2: Under Long-lived access tokens, choose Create token. Name it, for example LocalAI, and copy it. Home Assistant shows it only once.
setup.step3: Paste it here and write the address you use to open Home Assistant. The token has the rights of the user who made it: make it with a user who can see only what you want to share, if you can.
setup.step4: Leave the write mode on Read only until you have read the limits below. The add-on never operates locks, alarms, garage doors or sirens, whatever you choose.
setup.tls: Home Assistant with a self-signed certificate: pin its SHA-256 fingerprint in the section below. The add-on then accepts that one certificate for that one address and still checks everything else.

writeMode.label: What the agent may change in your home
writeMode.hint: Only the services on the allowlist below, on entities that are not excluded.

line.propose: Each change waits for your OK.
line.auto: Your chats switch lights and similar at once.

note.off: Write access is off: this connection only reads.
note.propose: Each change waits in your approvals until you confirm it.
note.auto: A chat of yours switches lights, switches and media at once, without asking. Anything with a physical effect, such as heating or a blind, a scene or a script, still waits for your confirmation every time. Runs without you present also wait.

policy.title: What chats may do in your home
policy.loadFailed: The limits could not be loaded.
policy.saveFailed: The limits could not be saved.
policy.intro: These limits apply to every Home Assistant connection of this server. The write mode of a connection decides whether a chat may change anything at all; these limits decide what.
policy.physical: A service you allow here can move a blind, heat a room, run a script or send a message. Allow only what you would let a stranger in your house do. Every service that is not a light, a switch, an input boolean or media playback waits for your confirmation each time, whatever the write mode is.
policy.readOnly: Only an administrator can change these limits.
policy.broken: The saved limits could not be read, so the tools refuse to work. Save the limits again to repair them.
policy.saved: Saved. The next call uses the new limits.
policy.allowHint: One per line, as domain.service, or domain.* for the services of a domain (the reload and restart services are never included). Anything not listed is refused.
policy.allowShape: "{{entry}}" is not written domain.service or domain.*.
policy.allowHard: "{{entry}}" can never be allowed. See the list of services that are never available.
policy.allowNone: Nothing is allowed: the write tools refuse every call.

class.quiet: Acts when the write mode allows

policy.confirmNote: These need your confirmation on every call: {{domains}}.
policy.maxTargetsHint: Between 1 and 20. A call names its entities one by one: areas, devices and all are not accepted.
policy.targetsShape: Enter a whole number from 1 to 20.
policy.excludeTitle: What the tools never show or touch
policy.excludeIntro: Excluded entities are left out of every search, state and history, and no call can switch them. Reading a lock is excluded by default; removing it from the list lets a chat read what the lock reports, never operate it.
policy.excludeDomainsHint: One per line, for example lock, alarm_control_panel, camera.
policy.excludeAreasHint: One per line, by name. The entities of these areas are hidden. If Home Assistant cannot answer which entities they are, the tools refuse instead of guessing.
policy.excludePatternsHint: One regular expression per line, matched against the whole entity ID, for example sensor\..*_bedroom.
policy.excludeLabelHint: Entities that carry this Home Assistant label are hidden. Leave it empty to turn the check off.
policy.pinsHint: For a self-signed certificate: host:port=fingerprint, one per line. The fingerprint is the SHA-256 of the certificate, 64 digits, with or without colons. Get it with openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256.
policy.pinShape: "{{entry}}" is not written host:port=fingerprint with a 64-digit SHA-256.
policy.hardIntro: The add-on refuses these whatever the settings are, and no model can change that: locks, alarms, sirens, valves, water heaters, cameras, restarts and reloads, shell commands, scripts of the system, and system and add-on management. Garage doors, gates, doors and covers of unknown type are never moved.

approval.title: Home Assistant: {{action}}
approval.asFirst: The first connection that lists this address
approval.asUnknown: A Home Assistant connection for this address
approval.cut: Shown cut. The whole value is sent.
approval.physical: This has a physical effect or runs automation in your home. It happens as soon as you confirm.
approval.quiet: This switches things in your home as soon as you confirm.
